registration: Registered in source/runtime/registry.mjs after entity-record after differential tests passed.
selection: All selected bodies are straight-line functions with at most eight WAT instructions and no call, call_indirect, branch, loop, or memory.grow. Three other candidates with call_indirect (1859, 2345, 4329) were deliberately excluded.
abi: Every hook preserves the original arity and result type. i32 parameters are normalized with >>>0 only for address formation; field and memarg offsets are added without wrapping, so an effective address at or above 2^32 traps. DataView range errors are converted to WebAssembly.RuntimeError("memory access out of bounds"). Loads and stores are little-endian and unaligned. Store order matches the WAT evaluation order, which matters for the vtable/copy helpers and for 2408/2631 where the field copy precedes the vtable store. Stack hooks read or write the exported stack-pointer global exactly as 3475/3364 do.

argumentRows: addresses at 0x3ffffff minus index (the last 64 MiB addresses)
validation.comparison: Every comparison asserts the return value or the trap constructor/message, all 67,108,864 bytes of linear memory, and the stack-pointer global. The arity test makes no oracle memory comparison. The three trapping rows in safe and overlap are the intentional unreachable functions 754, 1777, and 2491; zero adds the three dereference traps, and boundary adds forty-one more address-overflow traps.
limitations: The four argument rows are representative, not an exhaustive enumeration of 32-bit addresses or byte patterns.
The hooks are behaviorally equivalent replacements for shipped WASM bodies, not the original C++ source or original identifiers.
Recovered names describe observed constant, load/store, vtable, or stack behavior; they are not claims about the original class names.
These 74 leaves are a small fraction of the 4,081 remaining client functions and do not by themselves establish complete gameplay equivalence.
